children: Shipbuilder targets more than 550 white- and blue-collar hires by March 2027 as training programme builds a skilled maritime talent pipeline

Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (SDHI) has more than doubled its workforce over the past 18 months and plans to hire more than 550 employees by March 2027, as it expands shipbuilding, repair and heavy fabrication operations.

The hiring will span both white- and blue-collar roles across project management, design, supply chain, newbuild, repair and refit operations, as well as heavy fabrication and civil works. The company is also looking for specialised skilled workers in areas such as precision welding, fitting and pipework.

SDHI expects the expansion of its ongoing projects to generate at least 5,000 additional jobs over the next two to three years through vendors and supply-chain partners. This could extend the employment impact beyond the shipyard into the wider maritime manufacturing ecosystem.

The workforce expansion is being supported by SWAVALAMBAN, a structured training programme launched last year to develop industry-ready maritime talent. The programme combines sourcing, pre-onboarding, technical induction, mentorship and shop-floor deployment, with more than 100 graduate, postgraduate and diploma engineers and industrial technicians having completed training.

SDHI said the programme has reduced the time taken to move trainees from classroom learning to shop-floor deployment by at least 30 per cent. The initiative was developed with the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Indian Maritime University, Gujarat Maritime Board and 11 Industrial Training Institutes.

For the HR and talent ecosystem, the hiring push highlights the growing importance of industry-linked skilling in sectors where expansion depends on specialised technical capabilities. Rather than relying solely on experienced hires, SDHI is building a pipeline that combines formal training with practical exposure before employees move into operational roles.

The company’s plans also reflect the wider workforce requirements of India’s shipbuilding ambitions, where demand is expected to span engineers, project professionals and skilled trades alongside the supporting vendor and supply-chain workforce.
